channel.title: Web3 Hub
channel.description: Web3 Hub reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, exchanges, DeFi protocols, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and network upgrades.

item.title: Check Liquidity Before You Choose a Cross-Chain Bridge Route
item.description: A bridge quote is useful only if the route can fund its output; compare executable liquidity, fees and settlement risk across every step before signing.

item.title: How to Fund Gas After a Treasury Bridge Transfer
item.description: After a treasury bridge transfer, fund destination gas with its native token or a supported gas service, then verify the wallet can transact.

item.title: Fraud proofs keep invalid L2 withdrawals from reaching Ethereum
item.description: Fraud proofs let challengers dispute an optimistic rollup’s state before an L2 withdrawal reaches Ethereum; users then prove inclusion and finalize the exit.

item.title: Ethereum-to-Mantle deposits can wait at two different stages
item.description: An Ethereum-to-Mantle deposit can stay pending during Ethereum confirmation or Mantle message relay; the transaction hash shows which step is waiting and what to do next.

item.title: How to Move Tokens Before a Destination-Chain DAO Vote
item.description: A destination-chain DAO vote may require tokens to be present before its snapshot; check the voting rules, bridge early, and confirm which balance counts.

item.title: BSC Liquidity Adds Can Shift Prices Without Trade Volume
item.description: On BSC, added liquidity can deepen a pool without adding trade volume; reserve ratios, pool choice and chart settings explain why token prices can still move.

item.title: Polygon ERC-20 mapping links Ethereum tokens to Polygon copies
item.description: An ERC-20 reaches Polygon PoS through a mapped child contract: the bridge locks tokens on Ethereum, mints a matching balance, and reverses that flow on withdrawal.

item.title: Bridge Lockup Risk: How Cross-Chain Tokens Can Get Stuck
item.description: Bridge lockup risk is the chance that tokens on one chain become inaccessible or lose backing when a bridge fails, is exploited or cannot release them.

item.title: Block-Height Vesting Needs One Clock Across Chains
item.description: Block-height vesting releases tokens as a chain advances, but multi-chain schedules need one authoritative clock, verified updates and clear rules for delayed messages.

item.title: How to Reconcile Treasury Payouts Across Chains
item.description: Cross-chain payout reconciliation matches treasury debits to destination credits, using shared IDs and chain records to flag delays, failures and duplicates.

item.title: How Much USDC a Cross-Chain Swap Delivers
item.description: Your USDC payout depends on the route’s net quote, fees, slippage and token version; check the minimum received before approving a cross-chain swap.

item.title: Cross-Chain Swap Stuck? Check These Three Transaction Stages
item.description: Check the source transaction first, then the bridge status and destination wallet; each step points to a different fix and helps prevent duplicate swaps or lost fees.

item.title: Check the XMR route before sending funds to a bridge
item.description: Before sending XMR to a bridge, confirm the deposit network, exact asset, minimum, and destination wallet; the address may be a route endpoint, not your wallet.

item.title: How to Make a First XMR-to-zXMR Transfer
item.description: ZeroFi’s XMR-to-zXMR flow sends Monero to a deposit address and mints a token on Ethereum Sepolia; check the network, minimum and confirmation status before starting.

item.title: Token freezes can stop a TRON swap at the contract
item.description: A TRON token freeze can make a balance visible but unusable in a swap; the block usually comes from token contract rules, not TRON’s native staking freeze.

item.title: Check the Token and Router Before a TRON Swap
item.description: Find a TRON swap contract by matching the token address, checking the router and quote, then comparing liquidity, fees and execution risk before signing.

item.title: A fast bridge quote does not prove finality
item.description: A bridge's fast quote can reflect fronted liquidity, not settled source-chain finality; check confirmations, proof design and exit rules before moving assets.

item.title: How Bungee Handles Cross-Chain Token Swaps
item.description: Bungee combines token swaps and bridge routes in one quote; fees, delivery time and destination gas still depend on the route and chains you choose.

item.title: Wrapped and native tokens on Manta Pacific serve different roles
item.description: On Manta Pacific, a wrapped balance can represent an asset bridged from elsewhere, while a native token originates on the network; the contract address tells you which you hold.

item.title: Bridge Fees Can Buy Faster Withdrawals, at a Price
item.description: Paying a bridge fee can shorten a withdrawal by buying liquidity, but compare the total cost, route, settlement risk and destination chain before signing.
